messages:
nina: quick heads-up — ran a focused profile on the 1F1B workload with seq_len=1024 and saw a ~12% increase in pp-bubble time vs last week. flame attached: https://perf.redwood/fire/2287654321 :eyes:

sample notes: kernel selector picked the small-tile GEMM for a bunch of attention matmuls (shapes around 128x64) which causes longer kernel setup + launch overhead and hurts comm/compute overlap. kv-cache hit pattern is also weird — lots of partial cache misses that trigger extra all-reduces.

logs/snippet:
```
RT_PROF=1 ./run_infer --model bert-large --microbatch=16 --schedule=1f1b --seq_len=1024 --dump-kernel-decisions=kernel.decisions
cat kernel.decisions | grep matmul | sort -u
```

sam: looking. can you paste the profiler summary (wall/allreduce/compute) and the kernel.decisions tail? my guess is selector heuristics shifted after the last kernel-priority change. if it's the small-tile GEMM overhead we can force the 'wide-gemm' path for those dims as a quick probe. also try increasing microbatch to 24 to see batching amortization.

nina: pasted the profiler excerpt from the run:
```
wall_total: 1240ms
compute: 760ms
allreduce: 210ms
pp-bubble: 170ms  <-- inflated vs baseline (150ms)
kernel-overhead (launch/setup): ~40ms (notable)
```

kernel.decisions tail:
```
matmul(128,64) -> small_tile_gemm_v2
matmul(128,128) -> wide_gemm_opt
attn_ffwd(…) -> attentn_opt_v1
```

kai: two quick thoughts — 1) small_tile_gemm_v2 has a nontrivial per-launch latency; if microbatching is low we pay it repeatedly. bump microbatch to 24 or 32 and re-eval. 2) KV cache warmup: partial misses look like they fall into a path that performs a cross-host sync early. Add a lightweight prefix cache warmup run (empty prompt sweep) to populate KVs before hitting 1F1B steady-state.

pranav: ran an A/B on stage: override selector to prefer wide_gemm for matmul(128,64). results (avg over 50 steps):
```
A (baseline, micro=16): wall=1240ms, pp-bubble=170ms, tps=8.3
B (selector override): wall=1144ms, pp-bubble=130ms, tps=8.9
delta: -7.8% wall, -23% pp-bubble, +7% tps
allreduce time went up slightly (+5ms) but overall step improved
```

perf-bot: flamegraph & step breakdown uploaded: https://perf.redwood/fire/2287654321/flame.svg — kernel-launch hotspots highlighted, small_tile_gemm_v2 accounts for ~35% of kernel-overhead.

sam: nice signal. plan: 1) land a temporary runtime flag `--force-kernel=wide_gemm_for_matmul_128x64` behind a rollout gate; 2) run canary at 10% Dedicated for 2 hours; 3) collect per-route latency, token cost, and error-rate regressions (QA evals). I'll draft the flag patch and add a runtime toggle in the console.

nina: sounds good. two follow-ups: make sure the fallback path remains (if wide_gemm regresses for some tensor shapes we should auto-fallback after 3 failures). also attach a KV-cache warmup job before shifting traffic to minimize the early allreduce spikes.

sam: ack — will add fallback (attempts=3, degrade_to=small_tile_gemm_v2) and a health check that verifies comm/compute overlap > 40% on canary nodes. snippet for ops team: 
```yaml
runtime_overrides:
  kernel_for_shape:
    "matmul:128x64": wide_gemm_opt
  fallback_policy:
    attempts: 3
    degrade_to: small_tile_gemm_v2
```

nina: I'll create the rollout ticket and schedule the KV warmup job (30min empty prompts on canary pool) before enabling the kernel override. ticket/links: https://jira.redwood/ENG-PP-2287

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-19T03:00Z -> target: dedicated-canary-3 (10% traffic). will post results summary after run. :white_check_mark:

pranav: once canary runs I'll export perf traces and run the new microbatch sweep (16/24/32) to validate stability. initial numbers suggest microbatch=24 + kernel-override gives best win/risk tradeoff.

nina: perfect — thanks everyone. I'll consolidate notes and add a short postmortem entry if anything funky shows up. :thumbsup:
